docs.title: The Four Sections of a Robot File
docs.text:
A Robot Framework file can contain up to four sections. Each section header uses three asterisks (***) on both sides.

Section Purpose *** Settings *** Imports, metadata, suite/test lifecycle hooks *** Variables *** File-level variable declarations *** Test Cases *** The actual test cases (.robot files only) *** Keywords *** User-defined keywords (both .robot and .resource)

docs.title: 1. *** Settings ***
docs.text: Imports libraries and resource files, adds suite documentation, and configures setup/teardown hooks.

docs.title: 2. *** Variables ***
docs.text: Declares variables available throughout the file. Prefer this section over hardcoding values inside keywords.

docs.title: 3. *** Test Cases ***
docs.text: Where the actual tests are defined. A test case consists of a name (at the beginning of a line) and a series of keyword calls (indented with at least two spaces).

docs.title: 4. *** Keywords ***
docs.text: Custom sequences of existing keywords that simplify complex operations or promote code reuse.

docs.title: Fully Annotated Example
docs.text:
The following example shows a complete .robot file with all four sections and demonstrates real usage patterns:

# tests/login_tests.robot
# UTF-8 encoded — default for all Robot Framework files

*** Settings ***
Documentation       Test suite for user login functionality.
...                 Covers valid login, invalid credentials, and locked accounts.

Library             SeleniumLibrary
Resource            ../resources/common.resource
Resource            ../resources/login_page.resource

Suite Setup         Open Browser To Base URL
Suite Teardown      Close All Browsers
Test Setup          Navigate To Login Page
Test Teardown       Capture Page Screenshot On Failure

Metadata            Version    1.0
Metadata            Author     QA Team

*** Variables ***
${BASE_URL}         https://example.com
${BROWSER}          chrome
${VALID_USER}       admin
${VALID_PASS}       secret

*** Test Cases ***
Valid Login Navigates To Dashboard
    [Documentation]    Verifies that a user with valid credentials reaches the dashboard.
    [Tags]             smoke    login    positive
    Login As User      ${VALID_USER}    ${VALID_PASS}
    Page Should Contain    Welcome, ${VALID_USER}

Invalid Password Shows Error Message
    [Documentation]    Verifies that entering a wrong password shows a validation error.
    [Tags]             login    negative
    Login As User      ${VALID_USER}    wrongpassword
    Error Message Should Be Visible    Invalid username or password

*** Keywords ***
Login As User
    [Documentation]    Enters credentials and submits the login form.
    [Arguments]    ${username}    ${password}
    Input Text        id:username    ${username}
    Input Password    id:password    ${password}
    Click Button      id:login-btn

Error Message Should Be Visible
    [Arguments]    ${expected_message}
    Element Should Be Visible    css:.error-message
    Element Text Should Be       css:.error-message    ${expected_message}

Capture Page Screenshot On Failure
    Run Keyword If Test Failed    Capture Page Screenshot

docs.title: Indentation
docs.text:
Robot Framework uses spaces for indentation — not tabs. The minimum is two spaces between a keyword call and its arguments, and between items on the same line.

*** Test Cases ***
Example
    Log    Hello World          # two spaces between keyword and argument
    Should Be Equal    1    1   # two spaces between each argument

docs.title: The 2-Space Separator Rule
docs.text:
Robot Framework uses two or more spaces (or a pipe |) to separate tokens. A single space is treated as part of the token value, not as a separator.

# WRONG — "Log Hello World" is treated as one keyword name
Log Hello World

# CORRECT — two spaces separate the keyword "Log" from its argument
Log    Hello World

docs.title: Continuation Lines
docs.text:
Long keyword calls or settings can be split across multiple lines using ... as a continuation marker:

*** Settings ***
Documentation    This suite tests the login functionality
...              of the main application.
...              It covers both positive and negative scenarios.

*** Test Cases ***
Long Keyword Call
    Some Very Long Keyword Name
    ...    argument_one
    ...    argument_two
    ...    argument_three

docs.title: Comments
docs.text:
Use # for inline comments. Everything after # on a line is ignored by the parser.

*** Test Cases ***
Commented Example
    Log    Starting test    # this comment is ignored
    # This entire line is a comment
    Click Button    id:submit

docs.title: Suite Initialization Files
docs.text:
When a directory is treated as a test suite, you can add an __init__.robot file to that directory. This file sets up suite-level settings (e.g., Suite Setup, Suite Teardown, Documentation) that apply to all test files in the folder.

tests/
├── __init__.robot          # suite-level setup for the entire tests/ folder
├── login_tests.robot
└── checkout_tests.robot

# tests/__init__.robot
*** Settings ***
Documentation    Main test suite for the Example application.
Suite Setup      Start Application Server
Suite Teardown   Stop Application Server

Next: The Settings Section

docs.title: The Settings Section
docs.text: The *** Settings *** section is the control hub of your Robot Framework file. It tells the framework which tools to use, what metadata to include, and how to manage the test lifecycle.

docs.title: 1. Library
docs.text:
Used to import standard or external libraries. Library names are case-sensitive and must match the installed package exactly.

*** Settings ***
Library    OperatingSystem
Library    SeleniumLibrary
Library    RequestsLibrary
Library    Collections

docs.title: Library Aliasing (WITH NAME)
docs.text:
If you need to import two libraries that share keyword names, use WITH NAME to assign an alias:

*** Settings ***
Library    mypackage.module.DateUtils    WITH NAME    DateUtils
Library    anotherpackage.DateUtils      WITH NAME    AltDateUtils

Call keywords using the alias prefix:

*** Test Cases ***
Alias Example
    ${d1}=    DateUtils.Get Current Date
    ${d2}=    AltDateUtils.Get Current Date

docs.title: Library with Arguments
docs.text:
Some libraries accept constructor arguments:

*** Settings ***
Library    SeleniumLibrary    timeout=10    implicit_wait=0    run_on_failure=Capture Page Screenshot

docs.title: 2. Resource
docs.text:
Used to import external .resource files containing shared keywords and variables.

*** Settings ***
Resource    ../resources/common.resource
Resource    ../resources/login_page.resource

Paths are relative to the file containing the Resource setting. Use ${CURDIR} for paths that must be portable:

*** Settings ***
Resource    ${CURDIR}/../resources/common.resource

docs.title: 3. Variables
docs.text:
Imports an external variable file (a Python module or YAML file that defines variables).

*** Settings ***
Variables    ../data/config.py
Variables    ../data/test_users.yaml

Python variable file example (data/config.py):

BASE_URL = "https://example.com"
BROWSER = "chrome"
TIMEOUT = 10

YAML variable file example (data/test_users.yaml):

ADMIN_USER:
  username: admin
  password: secret

READONLY_USER:
  username: viewer
  password: viewonly

docs.title: 4. Documentation
docs.text:
Provides a high-level description of the test suite. This text appears in the execution logs and reports.

*** Settings ***
Documentation    Suite for testing the user registration flow.
...              Covers email validation, duplicate prevention, and confirmation emails.

docs.title: 5. Metadata
docs.text:
Adds custom metadata key-value pairs to the suite. Visible in report.html.

*** Settings ***
Metadata    Version       1.2.0
Metadata    Author        QA Team
Metadata    Environment   staging
Metadata    Jira          PROJ-1234

docs.title: 6. Suite Setup / Suite Teardown
docs.text:
Runs a keyword once before (setup) or after (teardown) all tests in the file.

*** Settings ***
Suite Setup       Initialize Database Connection
Suite Teardown    Close Database Connection

Use Run Keywords to call multiple keywords in a single setup or teardown:

*** Settings ***
Suite Setup    Run Keywords
...    Start Application Server
...    AND    Clear Test Data
...    AND    Create Default User

docs.title: 7. Test Setup / Test Teardown
docs.text:
Runs a keyword before/after every individual test case in the file. Can be overridden at the test case level.

*** Settings ***
Test Setup       Open Browser    ${BASE_URL}    ${BROWSER}
Test Teardown    Close Browser

docs.title: 8. Tags (Robot Framework 6+)
docs.text:
In Robot Framework 6, Force Tags and Default Tags were replaced by a single Test Tags setting:

*** Settings ***
Test Tags    regression    browser:chrome

Test Tags applies the listed tags to every test case in the suite.

[!NOTE] Force Tags and Default Tags still work in RF 6 but are deprecated. Migrate to Test Tags for new projects.

Legacy syntax (RF 4/5 — avoid in new projects):

*** Settings ***
Force Tags      regression
Default Tags    smoke

docs.title: 9. Test Template
docs.text:
Sets a default template keyword for all test cases in the file, enabling data-driven testing without repeating [Template] in each test.

*** Settings ***
Test Template    Verify Login Fails With

*** Variables ***
${URL}    https://example.com/login

*** Test Cases ***              USERNAME       PASSWORD
Invalid Username                bad_user       correct_pw
Invalid Password                admin          wrong_pw
Empty Username                  ${EMPTY}       secret
Empty Password                  admin          ${EMPTY}

*** Keywords ***
Verify Login Fails With
    [Arguments]    ${username}    ${password}
    Open Browser    ${URL}    chrome
    Input Text        id:username    ${username}
    Input Password    id:password    ${password}
    Click Button      id:login-btn
    Element Should Be Visible    css:.error-message
    [Teardown]    Close Browser

docs.title: 10. Test Timeout
docs.text:
Sets the maximum execution time for every test in the suite. Any test that exceeds this limit is marked as failed.

*** Settings ***
Test Timeout    2 minutes

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
The following shows all major settings in a single file:

*** Settings ***
Documentation    End-to-end tests for the checkout flow.
...              Requires a running application at ${BASE_URL}.

Library          SeleniumLibrary    timeout=15    run_on_failure=Capture Page Screenshot
Library          Collections
Resource         ../resources/common.resource
Resource         ../resources/checkout_page.resource
Variables        ../data/config.py

Metadata         Version       2.0.0
Metadata         Author        QA Team
Metadata         Ticket        PROJ-999

Suite Setup      Open Browser    ${BASE_URL}    ${BROWSER}
Suite Teardown   Close All Browsers

Test Setup       Navigate To Home Page
Test Teardown    Run Keyword If Test Failed    Log    Test failed: ${TEST NAME}

Test Tags        checkout    e2e
Test Timeout     3 minutes

[!IMPORTANT] Always use at least two spaces between a setting name and its value. A single space causes a parse error or unexpected behavior.

Next: Test Suites and Cases

docs.title: Test Suites and Cases
docs.text: Robot Framework provides flexible ways to organize and execute tests, whether they are individual files or grouped into suites and folders.

docs.title: Defining a Test Case
docs.text:
Test cases are defined in the *** Test Cases *** section.

  • Name: Must start at the beginning of the line (no leading spaces).
  • Body: Consists of keyword calls indented with at least two spaces.
*** Test Cases ***
My First Test
    Log    This is a test case

docs.title: Test Case Settings
docs.text:
Each test case can have its own settings, written as bracketed entries before or within the keyword body.

Setting Purpose [Documentation] Describes what the test verifies [Tags] Categorizes the test for filtering and reporting [Setup] Keyword to run before this specific test [Teardown] Keyword to run after this specific test (even if failed) [Timeout] Maximum execution time for this test [Template] Sets a keyword as the test template for data-driven tests 
*** Test Cases ***
User Can Log In With Valid Credentials
    [Documentation]    Verifies successful login and redirect to dashboard.
    [Tags]             smoke    login    priority:high
    [Setup]            Navigate To Login Page
    [Teardown]         Close Browser
    [Timeout]          1 minute
    Input Text        id:username    admin
    Input Password    id:password    secret
    Click Button      id:login-btn
    Location Should Contain    /dashboard

docs.title: Test Suites vs. Test Cases
docs.text:
• Test Case File: A single .robot file containing multiple test cases. When executed, it behaves as a single suite.
  • Test Suite (Folder): A directory containing multiple .robot files. Robot Framework treats the entire directory as a nested test suite hierarchy.

docs.title: Tags
docs.text:
Tags are free-form labels attached to test cases. They serve several purposes:

  • Selective execution: Run only tests with (or without) certain tags.
  • Reporting: Filter results by tag in report.html.
  • Documentation: Communicate intent (e.g., smoke, regression, WIP, jira:PROJ-123).
*** Test Cases ***
Add Item To Cart
    [Tags]    smoke    cart    positive
    ...

User Cannot Check Out With Empty Cart
    [Tags]    cart    negative    regression
    ...

docs.title: 1. Individual Test Files
docs.text:
Each functional area has its own .robot file.

tests/
├── login_tests.robot
├── checkout_tests.robot
└── search_tests.robot

docs.title: 2. Grouped Test Suites (Folders)
docs.text:
Large projects group related tests into folders. Each subfolder is a nested suite.

tests/
├── __init__.robot          # suite-level setup for all tests
├── ui/
│   ├── __init__.robot
│   ├── login_tests.robot
│   └── checkout_tests.robot
└── api/
    ├── __init__.robot
    └── user_api_tests.robot

docs.title: Data-Driven Test Cases with Templates
docs.text: A template replaces the keyword body of a test case with a single keyword. Each test case then provides only the data (arguments). This pattern is ideal for testing the same behavior with many input/output combinations.

docs.title: [Template] per Test Case
docs.text:
*** Test Cases ***
Login With Bad Credentials
    [Template]    Login Should Fail With Message
    invalid_user    correct_pw    Invalid username or password
    admin           wrong_pw      Invalid username or password
    ${EMPTY}        ${EMPTY}      Username is required

*** Keywords ***
Login Should Fail With Message
    [Arguments]    ${username}    ${password}    ${expected_msg}
    Input Text        id:username    ${username}
    Input Password    id:password    ${password}
    Click Button      id:login-btn
    Element Text Should Be    css:.error-msg    ${expected_msg}

docs.title: Suite-Level Test Template
docs.text:
Set the template once in *** Settings *** and define only data rows in *** Test Cases ***:

*** Settings ***
Test Template    Validate Form Field

*** Test Cases ***           FIELD_ID      VALUE         EXPECTED_ERROR
Empty Email Field            email         ${EMPTY}      Email is required
Invalid Email Format         email         notanemail    Enter a valid email
Email Too Long               email         ${'a' * 300}  Email is too long

*** Keywords ***
Validate Form Field
    [Arguments]    ${field_id}    ${value}    ${expected_error}
    Input Text     id:${field_id}    ${value}
    Click Button   id:submit
    Element Text Should Be    css:.field-error    ${expected_error}

docs.title: Running a Single File
docs.text: robot tests/login_tests.robot

docs.title: Running Multiple Files
docs.text: robot tests/login_tests.robot tests/checkout_tests.robot

docs.title: Running an Entire Folder
docs.text:
robot tests/

Robot Framework recursively finds and executes all .robot files in the folder.

docs.title: Selecting a Specific Suite
docs.text:
Use --suite (short: -s) to match suite names (case-insensitive, supports glob *):

robot --suite login_tests tests/
robot --suite "ui.*" tests/

docs.title: Selecting a Specific Test Case
docs.text:
Use --test (short: -t) to match test names:

robot --test "User Can Log In*" tests/
robot --test "Valid Login*" --test "Invalid Login*" tests/

docs.title: Filtering by Tag
docs.text:
# Run only smoke tests
robot --include smoke tests/

# Exclude work-in-progress tests
robot --exclude WIP tests/

# Run tests tagged smoke AND regression
robot --include smokeANDregression tests/

# Run tests tagged smoke OR regression
robot --include smokeORregression tests/

docs.title: Dry Run — Validate Without Executing
docs.text:
Check for syntax errors and missing keywords without running the tests:

robot --dryrun tests/

[!TIP] Group test cases that share the same libraries and resource files into the same suite file to improve maintainability and reduce library initialization overhead.

Next: Execution and Logging

docs.title: Execution and Logging
docs.text: Robot Framework provides powerful command-line options and an out-of-the-box reporting system that makes debugging straightforward.

docs.title: Basic Execution
docs.text:
# Run a single file
robot tests/login_tests.robot

# Run an entire folder
robot tests/

# Run with output in a dedicated directory
robot -d results tests/

docs.title: 1. Randomizing Order
docs.text:
To ensure test independence and avoid order-dependent failures, randomize execution order:

# Randomize the order of test cases within each suite
robot --randomize tests tests/

# Randomize suite execution order
robot --randomize suites tests/

# Randomize both
robot --randomize all tests/

docs.title: 2. Including/Excluding Tags
docs.text:
Tags allow you to run specific subsets of tests:

# Run only smoke tests
robot --include smoke tests/

# Exclude work-in-progress tests
robot --exclude WIP tests/

# Combine with AND (both tags required)
robot --include smokeANDcritical tests/

# Combine with OR (either tag matches)
robot --include smokeORcritical tests/

# Negate with NOT
robot --include smokeNOTslow tests/

[!NOTE] Tag logic operators (AND, OR, NOT) must be uppercase.

docs.title: 3. Log Levels
docs.text:
Control the verbosity of the generated log:

Level Description WARN Warnings and errors only INFO Standard execution info (default) DEBUG Detailed execution including all keyword calls TRACE Maximum detail — includes every argument and return value 
robot --loglevel DEBUG tests/
robot --loglevel TRACE tests/

Use TRACE when debugging unexpected argument values or return types.

docs.title: 4. Setting the Output Directory
docs.text:
Redirect all result files to a dedicated folder to keep the project root clean:

robot -d results tests/
robot --outputdir results tests/

docs.title: 5. Naming the Output Files
docs.text:
Customize the names of the generated files:

robot -d results \
    --output output.xml \
    --log log.html \
    --report report.html \
    tests/

docs.title: 6. Overriding Variables at the Command Line
docs.text:
Pass variable values directly on the command line to override those defined in the test file:

robot --variable BASE_URL:https://staging.example.com tests/
robot --variable BROWSER:firefox --variable TIMEOUT:30 tests/

This is especially useful in CI pipelines where environment-specific values differ between runs.

docs.title: 7. Dry Run — Syntax Validation
docs.text:
Run through the test structure without executing any keywords. Catches undefined keyword references and syntax errors:

robot --dryrun tests/

docs.title: 8. Running in Parallel with Pabot
docs.text:
For large test suites, use pabot to run suites in parallel:

pip install robotframework-pabot
pabot --processes 4 tests/

docs.title: Execution Flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Robot as Robot Framework Core
    participant TestData as Test Files (.robot)
    participant Output as output.xml
    participant Rebot as Rebot Tool
    participant HTML as log.html / report.html

    User->>Robot: Run `robot tests/`
    Robot->>TestData: Parse and Execute
    TestData-->>Robot: Execution Results
    Robot->>Output: Write raw XML data
    Robot->>Rebot: Trigger HTML generation
    Rebot->>Output: Read raw XML data
    Rebot->>HTML: Generate human-readable reports
    HTML-->>User: Open in Browser

docs.title: Interpreting Result Artifacts
docs.text: After every execution, Robot Framework generates three files in the output directory:

docs.title: 1. log.html
docs.text:
The most important file for debugging. It provides a hierarchical, step-by-step view of the execution.

  • Green: Keyword passed.
  • Red: Keyword failed.
  • Expand any keyword to see its arguments, return value, and any nested keyword calls.
  • Use the search bar at the top to filter by keyword name or message content.

docs.title: 2. report.html
docs.text:
A high-level summary suitable for sharing with stakeholders. Shows:

  • Total pass/fail counts
  • Pass rate percentage
  • Statistics by tag
  • Statistics by suite
  • Elapsed time

docs.title: 3. output.xml
docs.text: The raw execution data. This file is the source used to generate both HTML files. CI/CD tools (Jenkins, Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions) consume output.xml directly.

docs.title: Combining Reports with rebot
docs.text:
rebot post-processes one or more output.xml files and regenerates the HTML reports. This is useful for:

  • Merging results from parallel runs into one report.
  • Regenerating a report with different filtering settings without re-running tests.
# Merge multiple runs into one report
rebot -d results/merged results/run1/output.xml results/run2/output.xml

# Filter the merged report to only show failures
rebot --include FAILED results/output.xml

docs.title: GitHub Actions Example
docs.text:
# .github/workflows/robot.yml
name: Robot Framework Tests

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pip install -r requirements-rf.txt

      - name: Run Robot Framework tests
        run: robot --outputdir results --loglevel DEBUG tests/

      - name: Upload results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
        with:
          name: robot-results
          path: results/

docs.title: GitLab CI Example
docs.text:
# .gitlab-ci.yml
robot_tests:
  image: python:3.11
  script:
    - pip install -r requirements-rf.txt
    - robot --outputdir results tests/
  artifacts:
    when: always
    paths:
      - results/log.html
      - results/report.html
      - results/output.xml

docs.title: Debugging Failed Tests
docs.text:
1. Open log.html: Locate the red sections.
  2. Expand the failing keyword: See the exact step that failed and the error message.
  3. Check arguments: Use --loglevel TRACE to see the exact values passed to every keyword.
  4. Add temporary logging: Insert Log To Console DEBUG: ${var} to print variable states to the terminal in real time.
  5. Use --dryrun: Rule out syntax issues before running the full suite.

docs.title: Useful Debugging Keywords
docs.text:
*** Test Cases ***
Debug Example
    ${value}=    Get Text    id:price
    Log    Raw price value: ${value}         # appears in log.html
    Log To Console    Price = ${value}       # appears in terminal immediately
    Log Variables                            # logs ALL current variables to log.html

docs.title: Quick Reference
docs.text:
Flag Short Description --outputdir DIR -d DIR Set output directory --include TAG -i TAG Include tests with tag --exclude TAG -e TAG Exclude tests with tag --test NAME -t NAME Run specific test case --suite NAME -s NAME Run specific suite --loglevel LEVEL -L LEVEL Set log verbosity --variable NAME:VAL -v NAME:VAL Override variable --randomize TYPE Randomize order --dryrun Validate without executing

Next: Variables Deep Dive

docs.title: Variables Deep Dive
docs.text: Variables are essential for creating flexible, maintainable tests. They allow you to avoid hardcoding values like URLs, credentials, and web locators.

docs.title: 1. Scalar Variables (${scalar})
docs.text:
Used for a single value — a string, number, object, or return value from a keyword.

  • Declaration: ${MY_VAR} value
  • Usage: ${MY_VAR}
*** Variables ***
${BASE_URL}     https://example.com
${BROWSER}      chrome
${TIMEOUT}      10

*** Test Cases ***
Use Scalar Variable
    Open Browser    ${BASE_URL}    ${BROWSER}
    Set Browser Implicit Wait    ${TIMEOUT}

docs.title: 2. List Variables (@{list})
docs.text:
Used for ordered collections of values. Declaration uses @{} syntax, but individual items are always accessed with ${}.

  • Declaration: @{MY_LIST} item1 item2 item3
  • Accessing Items: ${MY_LIST}[0] returns item1 (0-indexed).
  • Iterating: Use in a FOR loop with @{MY_LIST}.
*** Variables ***
@{BROWSERS}    chrome    firefox    edge

*** Test Cases ***
Test In Multiple Browsers
    FOR    ${browser}    IN    @{BROWSERS}
        Open Browser    https://example.com    ${browser}
        Title Should Be    Example Domain
        Close Browser
    END

[!WARNING] In older versions of Robot Framework, list items were accessed with @{list}[index]. This syntax is deprecated. Always use ${list}[index] for individual items.

docs.title: 3. Dictionary Variables (&{dict})
docs.text:
Used for key-value pairs. Declaration uses &{} syntax; individual values are accessed with ${}.

  • Declaration: &{USER} username=admin password=secret
  • Accessing Items: ${USER}[username] returns admin.
*** Variables ***
&{ADMIN}     username=admin      password=secret
&{VIEWER}    username=viewer     password=readonly

*** Test Cases ***
Login As Admin
    Input Text        id:username    ${ADMIN}[username]
    Input Password    id:password    ${ADMIN}[password]
    Click Button      id:login-btn

docs.title: Built-In Variables
docs.text:
Robot Framework provides built-in variables automatically. You do not need to declare them.

Variable Value / Type Description ${EMPTY} "" An empty string ${SPACE} " " A single space character ${TRUE} True (bool) Boolean true ${FALSE} False (bool) Boolean false ${None} None Python None ${CURDIR} Path string Directory of the current file ${EXECDIR} Path string Directory where robot was invoked ${TEMPDIR} Path string System temporary directory ${TEST NAME} String Name of the currently running test ${SUITE NAME} String Name of the current suite ${TEST STATUS} PASS or FAIL Status of the current test (in teardown) ${OUTPUT DIR} Path string Directory where results are written 
*** Test Cases ***
Built-In Variables Example
    Should Be Equal    ${EMPTY}    ${EMPTY}
    Should Be True     ${TRUE}
    Log    Running test: ${TEST NAME} in suite: ${SUITE NAME}
    Log    Results go to: ${OUTPUT DIR}

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Access OS environment variables using %{VAR_NAME}:

*** Variables ***
${DB_PASSWORD}    %{DB_PASSWORD}

*** Test Cases ***
Use Environment Variable
    Log    DB password length: ${DB_PASSWORD.__len__()}

If the environment variable is not set, Robot Framework raises an error. Provide a default fallback:

robot --variable DB_PASSWORD:fallback_value tests/

docs.title: Variable Scope
docs.text:
Variables in Robot Framework have four scopes:

Scope Set With (Legacy) Set With (RF 7.0+) Visible To Local ${x}= keyword VAR ${x} value Current keyword only Test Set Test Variable VAR ${x} value scope=TEST All keywords in the current test Suite Set Suite Variable VAR ${x} value scope=SUITE All tests and keywords in the current suite Global Set Global Variable VAR ${x} value scope=GLOBAL All tests and suites in the run

[!TIP] New in Robot Framework 7.0: The native VAR syntax is now the recommended way to create variables dynamically, replacing the older Set Variable and Set * Variable keywords. It is more concise and clearly defines the scope.

*** Keywords ***
Set Up Shared State
    # Legacy approach:
    Set Test Variable    ${SESSION_ID}    abc-123

    # Modern RF 7.0+ approach:
    VAR    ${SESSION_ID}    abc-123    scope=TEST
    VAR    ${APP_BASE_URL}  https://staging.example.com    scope=SUITE
    VAR    ${ENV}           staging    scope=GLOBAL

docs.title: Dynamic Variables
docs.text:
Use the VAR syntax to assign a value to a variable at runtime:

*** Test Cases ***
Dynamic Variable Example
    ${today}=    Get Current Date    result_format=%Y-%m-%d
    Log    Today's date is ${today}

    VAR    ${count}    0
    ${count}=    Evaluate    ${count} + 1
    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${count}    1

docs.title: Using Evaluate for Expressions
docs.text:
Evaluate runs a Python expression and returns the result. It has access to standard Python modules:

*** Test Cases ***
Evaluate Examples
    ${pi}=       Evaluate    math.pi    modules=math
    ${upper}=    Evaluate    "hello".upper()
    ${items}=    Evaluate    [i * 2 for i in range(5)]
    Log    ${items}    # [0, 2, 4, 6, 8]

docs.title: Variable Files
docs.text: For large or environment-specific configurations, store variables in external Python or YAML files.

docs.title: Python Variable File
docs.text:
# data/config.py
BASE_URL = "https://example.com"
BROWSER = "chrome"
TIMEOUT = 15

# Complex variables work too
ADMIN_USER = {"username": "admin", "password": "secret"}

docs.title: YAML Variable File
docs.text:
# data/users.yaml
ADMIN_USER:
  username: admin
  password: secret

READONLY_USER:
  username: viewer
  password: view_only

Import in *** Settings ***:

*** Settings ***
Variables    ../data/config.py
Variables    ../data/users.yaml

Or pass at the command line:

robot --variablefile data/staging_config.py tests/

docs.title: Overriding Variables at the Command Line
docs.text:
Variables can be overridden when running tests without modifying any file:

robot --variable BASE_URL:https://staging.example.com tests/
robot --variable BROWSER:firefox --variable TIMEOUT:30 tests/

Command-line --variable values take precedence over *** Variables *** section values and variable files.

docs.title: 1. Centralize Web Locators
docs.text:
Store locators in variables so they only need updating in one place:

*** Variables ***
${USERNAME_INPUT}     id:username
${PASSWORD_INPUT}     id:password
${LOGIN_BUTTON}       id:login-btn
${ERROR_MESSAGE}      css:.error-message

docs.title: 2. Naming Conventions
docs.text:
Use descriptive, UPPER_CASE names for global and suite-level variables:

  • ${BASE_URL}, ${BROWSER}, ${ADMIN_USER}

Use lower_case or camelCase for local variables inside keywords:

  • ${response}, ${currentUser}, ${item_count}

docs.title: 3. Avoid Hardcoding Sensitive Data
docs.text:
Never hardcode passwords or API keys in .robot files. Use environment variables or an external secrets manager:

*** Variables ***
${API_KEY}    %{API_KEY}

[!NOTE] The 2-space rule is critical here too. Always use at least two spaces between the variable name and its value in the *** Variables *** section.

Next: User-Defined Keywords

docs.title: User-Defined Keywords
docs.text: User keywords are the building blocks of modular and readable Robot Framework tests. They allow you to combine multiple lower-level actions into a single, high-level business action.

docs.title: Creating a Keyword
docs.text:
Keywords are defined in the *** Keywords *** section.

*** Keywords ***
Log My Username and Password
    Log    Username: ${USER}[username]
    Log    Password: ${USER}[password]

docs.title: Keyword Settings
docs.text:
Each keyword definition can include the following settings:

Setting Purpose [Documentation] Describes what the keyword does (shown in log and IDE hover) [Arguments] Declares the keyword's parameters [Tags] Categorizes the keyword (useful for documentation generators) [Timeout] Maximum execution time [Teardown] Keyword to run after the main body, even if the body fails [Return] Legacy return syntax (use RETURN in RF 5+) 
*** Keywords ***
Open Login Page And Verify Title
    [Documentation]    Opens the login URL and asserts the page title.
    [Tags]             navigation    login
    [Timeout]          30 seconds
    Open Browser    ${BASE_URL}/login    ${BROWSER}
    Title Should Be    Login — Example App

docs.title: Nesting Keywords
docs.text:
You can call other keywords inside a user keyword, creating layers of abstraction:

flowchart TD
    A[Perform Login] --> B[Open Browser To Login Page]
    A --> C[Submit Credentials]
    A --> D[Verify Login Success]

    C --> E[Input Text: username]
    C --> F[Input Password: password]
    C --> G[Click Button: login-btn]
*** Keywords ***
Perform Login
    Open Browser To Login Page
    Submit Credentials
    Verify Login Success

Submit Credentials
    Input Text        id:username    ${USERNAME}
    Input Password    id:password    ${PASSWORD}
    Click Button      id:login-btn

Verify Login Success
    Location Should Contain    /dashboard
    Page Should Contain        Welcome

docs.title: Keywords with Arguments
docs.text: Arguments make keywords reusable across different scenarios.

docs.title: Defining Arguments
docs.text:
*** Keywords ***
Log Specific Data
    [Arguments]    ${data}
    Log    The data is: ${data}

docs.title: Multiple Arguments
docs.text:
*** Keywords ***
Login With Credentials
    [Arguments]    ${username}    ${password}
    Input Text        id:username    ${username}
    Input Password    id:password    ${password}
    Click Button      id:login-btn

docs.title: Default Argument Values
docs.text:
Provide a default using ${arg}=default_value. Arguments with defaults are optional when calling the keyword.

*** Keywords ***
Open App In Browser
    [Arguments]    ${url}=${BASE_URL}    ${browser}=chrome    ${maximize}=${TRUE}
    Open Browser    ${url}    ${browser}
    Run Keyword If    ${maximize}    Maximize Browser Window

Calling the keyword:

*** Test Cases ***
Open With Defaults
    Open App In Browser                              # all defaults used

Open Custom URL
    Open App In Browser    url=https://staging.example.com    browser=firefox

docs.title: Variable-Length Arguments (@{varargs})
docs.text:
Use @{args} to accept any number of positional arguments:

*** Keywords ***
Log All Values
    [Arguments]    @{values}
    FOR    ${v}    IN    @{values}
        Log    ${v}
    END

*** Test Cases ***
Pass Many Args
    Log All Values    apple    banana    cherry    date

docs.title: Keyword Arguments (&{kwargs})
docs.text:
Use &{kwargs} to accept named arguments as a dictionary:

*** Keywords ***
Create User With Options
    [Arguments]    ${username}    &{options}
    Log    Creating ${username}
    Log    Role: ${options.get('role', 'user')}
    Log    Email: ${options.get('email', 'no-reply@example.com')}

*** Test Cases ***
Create Admin User
    Create User With Options    alice    role=admin    email=alice@example.com

docs.title: RETURN (Robot Framework 5+, standard in 7+)
docs.text:
Use the RETURN statement to return a value from a keyword. Execution of the keyword stops at RETURN.

*** Keywords ***
Get Page Title Text
    ${title}=    Get Title
    RETURN    ${title}

Get Cart Item Count
    [Arguments]    ${expected_min}=0
    ${count_text}=    Get Text    css:.cart-count
    ${count}=         Convert To Integer    ${count_text}
    IF    ${count} < ${expected_min}
        Fail    Cart has fewer items than expected: ${count} < ${expected_min}
    END
    RETURN    ${count}

Calling a keyword that returns a value:

*** Test Cases ***
Verify Page Title
    ${title}=    Get Page Title Text
    Should Contain    ${title}    Dashboard

docs.title: [Return] (Legacy, Deprecated)
docs.text:
*** Keywords ***
Get Current Timestamp
    ${ts}=    Get Current Date    result_format=epoch
    [Return]    ${ts}

[!WARNING] Deprecated: The [Return] setting is officially deprecated in Robot Framework 7.0. It is highly recommended to migrate all old code to use the RETURN statement.

docs.title: Error Handling with TRY / EXCEPT
docs.text:
Use structured error handling to recover from expected failures:

*** Keywords ***
Click Button If Visible
    [Arguments]    ${locator}
    TRY
        Click Button    ${locator}
    EXCEPT    Element with locator '${locator}' not found*    type=glob
        Log    Button not found — skipping    WARN
    END

Fetch With Retry
    [Arguments]    ${url}    ${retries}=3
    FOR    ${i}    IN RANGE    ${retries}
        TRY
            ${resp}=    GET On Session    api    ${url}
            RETURN    ${resp}
        EXCEPT
            Log    Attempt ${i + 1} failed, retrying...    WARN
        END
    END
    Fail    All ${retries} attempts to GET ${url} failed

docs.title: Keyword Teardown
docs.text:
A keyword can define its own teardown, which runs even if the keyword body fails:

*** Keywords ***
Login And Take Screenshot
    [Teardown]    Capture Page Screenshot
    Input Text        id:username    admin
    Input Password    id:password    secret
    Click Button      id:login-btn
    Location Should Contain    /dashboard

docs.title: Local Variables
docs.text:
Variables created inside a keyword body are local to that keyword. They do not affect variables of the same name in the caller or in *** Variables ***.

*** Keywords ***
Demonstrate Local Scope
    ${result}=    Set Variable    local_value
    Log    Inside keyword: ${result}
    # ${result} does not exist outside this keyword

docs.title: Error Handling: Argument Mismatch
docs.text:
Robot Framework enforces argument counts strictly.

  • Keyword expects 2 arguments but receives 1: Keyword 'Login With Credentials' expected 2 arguments, got 1.

  • Keyword expects 2 arguments but receives 3: Keyword 'Login With Credentials' expected 2 arguments, got 3.

Always verify the [Arguments] definition matches your call sites.

[!TIP] Keep your keywords focused. A keyword with more than 10–15 steps is a sign it should be split into smaller sub-keywords. Each keyword should do exactly one thing at the right level of abstraction.

Next: Resource Files

docs.title: Resource Files
docs.text: Resource files (.resource) are the key to building large-scale, maintainable automation projects. They allow you to centralize keywords and variables, making them available to multiple test suites.

docs.title: Why Use Resource Files?
docs.text:
Without resource files, you would copy and paste common keywords (like Login) into every .robot file. If the login logic changes, you must update every file.

With a resource file, you update the logic in one place and all suites that import it are updated automatically.

docs.title: Creating a Resource File
docs.text:
A resource file looks like a .robot file but cannot contain a *** Test Cases *** section.

# resources/common.resource

*** Settings ***
Library    SeleniumLibrary

*** Variables ***
${BASE_URL}      https://example.com
${BROWSER}       chrome

*** Keywords ***
Open App
    Open Browser    ${BASE_URL}    ${BROWSER}
    Maximize Browser Window

Close App
    Close All Browsers

docs.title: Importing a Resource File
docs.text:
Use the Resource setting in *** Settings ***.

# tests/login_tests.robot

*** Settings ***
Resource    ../resources/common.resource

*** Test Cases ***
Example Test
    Open App
    Title Should Be    Example Domain
    [Teardown]    Close App

docs.title: Portable Paths with ${CURDIR}
docs.text:
To make imports work regardless of where robot is invoked, use ${CURDIR}:

*** Settings ***
Resource    ${CURDIR}/../resources/common.resource

${CURDIR} always resolves to the directory of the file containing the statement.

docs.title: Organizing Large Projects with Multiple Resource Files
docs.text:
Split resource files by page or domain concept — this is the Page Object Pattern for Robot Framework:

resources/
├── common.resource         # shared setup/teardown, browser helpers
├── login_page.resource     # locators and keywords for the login page
├── dashboard.resource      # locators and keywords for the dashboard
├── checkout.resource       # locators and keywords for checkout flow
└── api_helpers.resource    # RequestsLibrary session setup and shared API calls

docs.title: common.resource — Shared Lifecycle
docs.text:
# resources/common.resource

*** Settings ***
Library    SeleniumLibrary    timeout=15    run_on_failure=Capture Page Screenshot
Library    RequestsLibrary

*** Variables ***
${BASE_URL}      https://example.com
${BROWSER}       chrome
${API_URL}       https://api.example.com

*** Keywords ***
Open Browser To Base URL
    Open Browser    ${BASE_URL}    ${BROWSER}
    Maximize Browser Window

Close All Sessions
    Close All Browsers
    Delete All Sessions

docs.title: login_page.resource — Page-Specific Keywords
docs.text:
# resources/login_page.resource

*** Settings ***
Resource    common.resource

*** Variables ***
${USERNAME_INPUT}    id:username
${PASSWORD_INPUT}    id:password
${LOGIN_BUTTON}      id:login-btn
${ERROR_MESSAGE}     css:.error-message

*** Keywords ***
Navigate To Login Page
    Go To    ${BASE_URL}/login
    Title Should Be    Login

Login As
    [Arguments]    ${username}    ${password}
    Input Text        ${USERNAME_INPUT}    ${username}
    Input Password    ${PASSWORD_INPUT}    ${password}
    Click Button      ${LOGIN_BUTTON}

Login Error Should Be
    [Arguments]    ${expected_text}
    Element Should Be Visible    ${ERROR_MESSAGE}
    Element Text Should Be       ${ERROR_MESSAGE}    ${expected_text}

docs.title: Using Both in a Test Suite
docs.text:
# tests/login_tests.robot

*** Settings ***
Resource    ../resources/login_page.resource

Suite Setup       Open Browser To Base URL
Suite Teardown    Close All Sessions
Test Setup        Navigate To Login Page

*** Test Cases ***
Valid Login Redirects To Dashboard
    [Tags]    smoke    login
    Login As    admin    secret
    Location Should Contain    /dashboard

Invalid Password Shows Error
    [Tags]    login    negative
    Login As    admin    wrongpassword
    Login Error Should Be    Invalid username or password

docs.title: Variable Files
docs.text: For large or environment-specific data, use Python or YAML variable files instead of hardcoding in resource files.

docs.title: Python Variable File
docs.text:
# data/config.py
BASE_URL = "https://example.com"
BROWSER = "chrome"
TIMEOUT = 15

docs.title: YAML Variable File
docs.text:
# data/environments.yaml
STAGING:
  BASE_URL: https://staging.example.com
  API_URL: https://staging-api.example.com

PRODUCTION:
  BASE_URL: https://example.com
  API_URL: https://api.example.com

Import in Settings:

*** Settings ***
Variables    ${CURDIR}/../data/config.py

Or pass at the command line to switch environments:

robot --variablefile data/staging_config.py tests/
robot --variablefile data/production_config.py tests/

docs.title: Visibility and Inheritance
docs.text:
• Libraries: Importing a library in a resource file makes that library's keywords available to any test suite that imports the resource.
  • Variables: All variables declared in a resource file are available to the importing test suite and all other resource files it imports.
  • Keywords: All keywords in the resource file are available to the importing test suite.
  • Transitive imports: If resource_a.resource imports resource_b.resource, any test suite that imports resource_a also gains access to everything in resource_b.

[!NOTE] In the execution log.html, Robot Framework shows which file each keyword came from (e.g., login_page.Login As). This makes it easy to trace the source of a failing keyword.

docs.title: Shared Setup and Teardown Resource
docs.text:
A common pattern is to centralize suite setup and teardown in a shared resource:

# resources/lifecycle.resource

*** Settings ***
Library    SeleniumLibrary
Library    RequestsLibrary

*** Keywords ***
Start Test Suite
    [Arguments]    ${url}=${BASE_URL}    ${browser}=${BROWSER}
    Open Browser    ${url}    ${browser}
    Maximize Browser Window
    Create Session    api    ${API_URL}

End Test Suite
    Close All Browsers
    Delete All Sessions

Use it across any suite:

*** Settings ***
Resource    ../resources/lifecycle.resource

Suite Setup       Start Test Suite
Suite Teardown    End Test Suite

Next: Best Practices

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text: To build a scalable and maintainable automation suite, follow these industry-standard best practices.

docs.title: 1. Modularization with Resource Files
docs.text:
Never put all your logic in a single file. Centralize reusable keywords and variables in .resource files. This ensures that a change in the application (like a URL update) only needs to be made in one place.

resources/
├── common.resource         # lifecycle helpers (open/close browser, sessions)
├── login_page.resource     # login page locators and keywords
├── dashboard.resource      # dashboard locators and keywords
└── api_helpers.resource    # API session setup and shared request helpers

See Resource Files for a full example.

docs.title: 2. Page Object Pattern (POM)
docs.text:
Organize resource files by page or functional module:

  • login_page.resource — locators and keywords specific to the login page
  • dashboard.resource — locators and keywords for the dashboard
  • checkout.resource — locators and keywords for the checkout flow

Each page resource file declares its own locator variables in *** Variables *** and exposes business-level keywords in *** Keywords ***. Test cases import the page resource and call the keywords — they never touch locators directly.

# resources/checkout.resource

*** Variables ***
${CART_ICON}         css:.cart-icon
${CHECKOUT_BTN}      id:checkout-btn
${ORDER_CONFIRM}     css:.order-confirmation

*** Keywords ***
Proceed To Checkout
    Click Element    ${CART_ICON}
    Click Button     ${CHECKOUT_BTN}

Order Confirmation Should Be Visible
    Element Should Be Visible    ${ORDER_CONFIRM}

docs.title: 3. Clear Separation: "What" vs. "How"
docs.text:
Test cases should describe business logic (What). Keywords handle technical implementation (How).

# BAD — test case contains implementation details
*** Test Cases ***
Checkout Flow
    Click Element    css:.cart-icon
    Click Button     id:checkout-btn
    Wait Until Element Is Visible    css:.order-confirmation
    Element Text Should Be           css:.order-confirmation    Order placed!

# GOOD — test case reads as a business specification
*** Test Cases ***
Checkout Flow
    [Tags]    smoke    checkout
    Add Product To Cart    laptop
    Proceed To Checkout
    Complete Payment With    visa    4111111111111111
    Order Confirmation Should Be Visible

docs.title: 4. Descriptive Naming
docs.text:
• Test Cases: Readable sentences that describe what is being verified.
  • Invalid login should show error message
  • User can add product to cart
  • Keywords: "Verb + Object" style.
  • Login As, Click Logout Button, Verify Dashboard Is Visible
  • Variables: UPPER_CASE for suite/global scope; lower_case for local.
  • ${BASE_URL}, ${BROWSER}, local ${response}, ${item_count}
  • Files: Use snake_case and descriptive names.
  • login_tests.robot, checkout_page.resource

docs.title: 5. Avoid Hardcoding
docs.text:
Use the *** Variables *** section or external variable files for environment-specific data:

# BAD
Open Browser    https://example.com    chrome

# GOOD
*** Variables ***
${BASE_URL}    https://example.com
${BROWSER}     chrome

Open Browser    ${BASE_URL}    ${BROWSER}

For multi-environment setups, use separate variable files and pass them at runtime:

robot --variablefile data/staging.py tests/
robot --variablefile data/production.py tests/

docs.title: 6. Proper Use of Setup and Teardown
docs.text:
• Use Suite Setup for one-time initializations (start server, open browser).
  • Use Suite Teardown for cleanup that must happen once (stop server, close browser).
  • Use Test Teardown for per-test cleanup — it runs even if the test fails, ensuring a clean state for the next test.
*** Settings ***
Suite Setup      Open Browser    ${BASE_URL}    ${BROWSER}
Suite Teardown   Close All Browsers
Test Teardown    Run Keywords
...    Run Keyword If Test Failed    Capture Page Screenshot
...    AND    Clear Cookies

docs.title: 7. Tagging for Strategy
docs.text:
Categorize your tests to enable selective execution:

Tag Usage smoke Quick sanity check — runs on every commit regression Full suite — runs nightly or before a release critical Tests covering the most business-critical paths WIP Work in progress — excluded from CI slow Long-running tests — excluded from quick feedback loops jira:PROJ-123 Links to a specific ticket 
# Run only smoke tests on every push
robot --include smoke tests/

# Run regression suite overnight
robot --include regression tests/

# Skip slow and WIP tests
robot --exclude slow --exclude WIP tests/

docs.title: 8. Data-Driven Testing
docs.text:
Use templates for scenarios with many input combinations:

*** Settings ***
Test Template    Registration Should Fail With

*** Test Cases ***            EMAIL              PASSWORD        EXPECTED_ERROR
Empty Email                   ${EMPTY}           valid_pw        Email is required
Invalid Email Format          notanemail         valid_pw        Enter a valid email
Short Password                user@ex.com        ab              Password too short
Mismatched Passwords          user@ex.com        valid_pw        Passwords do not match

*** Keywords ***
Registration Should Fail With
    [Arguments]    ${email}    ${password}    ${expected_error}
    Go To          ${BASE_URL}/register
    Input Text     id:email       ${email}
    Input Text     id:password    ${password}
    Click Button   id:register-btn
    Element Text Should Be    css:.form-error    ${expected_error}

docs.title: 9. Custom Python Libraries for Complex Logic
docs.text:
When keyword logic requires conditional branching, loops, or external integrations that are cumbersome to express in Robot syntax, implement it as a Python library:

# libraries/ApiUtils.py
import requests

class ApiUtils:
    """Utility keywords for API testing."""

    def get_auth_token(self, base_url, username, password):
        """Authenticates and returns the JWT bearer token."""
        response = requests.post(
            f"{base_url}/auth/token",
            json={"username": username, "password": password},
            timeout=10,
        )
        response.raise_for_status()
        return response.json()["access_token"]

    def decode_jwt_payload(self, token):
        """Decodes a JWT payload without verifying the signature."""
        import base64, json
        payload = token.split(".")[1]
        # Add padding
        payload += "=" * (4 - len(payload) % 4)
        return json.loads(base64.b64decode(payload))

*** Settings ***
Library    ../libraries/ApiUtils.py

*** Test Cases ***
Admin Token Contains Admin Role
    ${token}=      Get Auth Token    ${API_URL}    admin    secret
    ${payload}=    Decode JWT Payload    ${token}
    Should Be Equal    ${payload}[role]    admin

docs.title: 10. Version Control
docs.text:
Always use Git. Exclude generated artifacts from the repository:

results/
output.xml
log.html
report.html
.venv/
__pycache__/
*.pyc

Commit meaningful messages when adding test cases:

test(login): add negative test for locked account
test(checkout): add data-driven payment validation tests
fix(login_page): update locator for username input after UI redesign

docs.title: 11. CI/CD Integration
docs.text:
Run tests automatically on every push or pull request. See the Execution and Logging page for complete GitHub Actions and GitLab CI examples.

Key CI practices:

  • Always pass --outputdir results to keep artifacts in one place.
  • Upload results/ as a build artifact so log.html is accessible after the run.
  • Use --loglevel DEBUG in CI for detailed failure diagnostics.
  • Use --variable BASE_URL:${{ env.STAGING_URL }} to inject environment-specific values.

Next: Troubleshooting

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Automation projects often run into similar issues. This guide covers the most common problems and their solutions.

docs.title: The "One Space" Mistake
docs.text:
Robot Framework requires at least two spaces (or a tab) between a keyword and its arguments. A single space makes Robot treat the whole line as one keyword name.

  • Problem: No keyword with name 'Log Hello World' found.
  • Cause: Log Hello World — only one space between Log and its argument.
  • Fix: Use two spaces: Log Hello World
# WRONG
Log Hello World

# CORRECT
Log    Hello World

docs.title: Deprecated List/Dict Syntax
docs.text:
• Problem: Warning Accessing list variable as scalar is deprecated.
  • Cause: Using @{list}[index] to access an individual item.
  • Fix: Always use ${list}[index] for individual items.
# WRONG (deprecated)
Log    @{MY_LIST}[0]

# CORRECT
Log    ${MY_LIST}[0]

docs.title: Continuation Marker Indentation
docs.text:
• Problem: Non-default argument after default arguments. or unexpected parse errors on multi-line definitions.
  • Cause: The ... continuation marker must be at the same indentation level as the line it continues.
# WRONG — continuation at wrong level
*** Settings ***
Resource    ../resources/common.resource
  ...    ../resources/login_page.resource

# CORRECT
*** Settings ***
Resource    ../resources/common.resource
...         ../resources/login_page.resource

docs.title: robot Command Not Recognized
docs.text:
• Problem: 'robot' is not recognized as an internal or external command.
  • Diagnosis:
pip show robotframework      # check if installed
python -m robot --version    # try invoking via python module
  • Fix:
  • If not installed: pip install robotframework
  • If installed but not in PATH: add C:\Python3xx\Scripts to your system's Path environment variable.
  • Alternatively, always invoke as python -m robot tests/.

docs.title: Library Import Failure
docs.text:
• Problem: Importing library 'SeleniumLibrary' failed: No module named 'SeleniumLibrary'
  • Causes and fixes:
Cause Fix Library not installed pip install robotframework-seleniumlibrary Wrong name in settings Check case: SeleniumLibrary not seleniumlibrary Wrong virtual environment active Activate the correct .venv first Library installed globally, but test runs inside .venv Install inside the venv: .venv\Scripts\pip install robotframework-seleniumlibrary

docs.title: Resource File Not Found
docs.text:
• Problem: Resource file '../resources/common.resource' does not exist.
  • Fix: Verify the path is relative to the file containing the Resource statement, not relative to the working directory. Use ${CURDIR} for portability:
*** Settings ***
Resource    ${CURDIR}/../resources/common.resource

docs.title: Module Not Found for Custom Library
docs.text:
• Problem: Importing library '../libraries/MyLib.py' failed.
  • Fix: Either use an absolute path, or add the library directory to Python's path using --pythonpath:
robot --pythonpath libraries tests/

Or set PYTHONPATH in the environment:

set PYTHONPATH=%CD%\libraries    # Windows CMD
$env:PYTHONPATH = "$PWD\libraries"  # Windows PowerShell
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD/libraries"  # macOS/Linux

docs.title: 3. Argument Mismatches
docs.text:
• Problem: Keyword 'Login With Credentials' expected 2 arguments, got 1.
  • Fix: Count the [Arguments] in the keyword definition and match them in the call.
# Keyword definition expects 2 arguments
*** Keywords ***
Login With Credentials
    [Arguments]    ${username}    ${password}
    ...

# WRONG — only 1 argument passed
Login With Credentials    admin

# CORRECT — 2 arguments passed
Login With Credentials    admin    secret

docs.title: ChromeDriver Version Mismatch
docs.text:
• Problem: SessionNotCreatedException: Message: session not created: This version of ChromeDriver only supports Chrome version XX
  • Fix (Option 1): Use Selenium 4.6+ with built-in Selenium Manager — it auto-downloads the correct driver. No manual driver management needed.
  • Fix (Option 2): Use webdriver-manager to auto-manage drivers:
# conftest.py or a setup keyword
from webdriver_manager.chrome import ChromeDriverManager
from selenium import webdriver
driver = webdriver.Chrome(ChromeDriverManager().install())
  • Fix (Option 3): Manually download ChromeDriver matching your Chrome version from chromedriver.chromium.org and add it to PATH.

docs.title: Browser Not Opening (Headless Environments)
docs.text:
• Problem: Tests fail immediately with a browser error in CI (no display).
  • Fix: Use headless mode:
*** Keywords ***
Open Browser Headless
    ${options}=    Evaluate    sys.modules['selenium.webdriver'].ChromeOptions()    modules=sys
    Call Method    ${options}    add_argument    --headless
    Call Method    ${options}    add_argument    --no-sandbox
    Call Method    ${options}    add_argument    --disable-dev-shm-usage
    Create Webdriver    Chrome    options=${options}
    Go To    ${BASE_URL}

Or use the simpler options argument available in newer SeleniumLibrary versions:

Open Browser    ${BASE_URL}    chrome    options=add_argument("--headless")

docs.title: Element Not Found / Timing Issues
docs.text:
• Problem: Element with locator 'id:submit' not found.
  • Cause: The element is not yet present in the DOM when the keyword runs.
  • Fix: Use explicit waits instead of Sleep:
# BAD — brittle timing
Sleep    3s
Click Button    id:submit

# GOOD — waits up to the implicit timeout
Wait Until Element Is Visible    id:submit
Click Button    id:submit

# BETTER — combined
Wait Until Element Is Enabled    id:submit    timeout=10s
Click Button    id:submit

docs.title: Session Not Found
docs.text:
• Problem: No session created with alias 'my_api'.
  • Cause: Create Session was not called before using GET On Session / POST On Session.
  • Fix: Call Create Session in Suite Setup or before the request:
*** Settings ***
Suite Setup    Create Session    my_api    ${API_URL}

*** Test Cases ***
Get Users
    ${resp}=    GET On Session    my_api    /users
    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${resp.status_code}    200

docs.title: SSL Certificate Errors
docs.text:
• Problem: SSLError: certificate verify failed
  • Fix (for non-production testing only): Disable SSL verification:
Create Session    my_api    ${API_URL}    verify=${FALSE}

docs.title: Variable Not Defined
docs.text:
• Problem: Variable '${MY_VAR}' not found.
  • Causes:
  • Typo in the variable name.
  • Variable set in a keyword but used outside its scope. See Variable Scope.
  • Variable file not imported.

docs.title: Environment Variable Not Set
docs.text:
• Problem: Environment variable 'DB_PASSWORD' not found.
  • Fix: Set the environment variable before running, or provide a fallback via --variable:
robot --variable DB_PASSWORD:test_password tests/

docs.title: 7. RF Version Incompatibilities
docs.text:
Symptom Likely Cause Fix RETURN causes syntax error Using RF < 5.0 Upgrade RF or use [Return] TRY/EXCEPT causes syntax error Using RF < 5.0 Upgrade RF Test Tags is ignored Using RF < 6.0 Upgrade RF or use Force Tags @{list}[index] deprecation warning Using old syntax Change to ${list}[index]

Check your version:

robot --version

Upgrade:

pip install --upgrade robotframework

docs.title: Debugging Workflow
docs.text:
1. Open log.html: Find the red (failing) keyword.
  2. Expand the keyword: Read the exact error message and the arguments passed.
  3. Use TRACE level: Re-run with --loglevel TRACE to see every argument and return value.
  4. Log variables: Add Log Variables to your keyword to dump all in-scope variables.
  5. Log to console: Add Log To Console DEBUG: ${var} for real-time terminal output.
  6. Dry run: Use --dryrun to catch undefined keyword references before execution.
*** Keywords ***
Debug Step
    Log Variables                                  # dump all variables to log
    Log To Console    \n--- Current URL: ${URL}    # terminal output
    Capture Page Screenshot                        # screenshot at this point
